summary: Phase 3 scenario generation for mo-execute-and-fulfill. 22 scenarios targeting the highest-stakes contract surfaces: three distinct 409 surfaces (pick stock_shortage, pick requirement_violation, ship negativeStock), the wait-for-MO 409 (same SalesError payload as plain shortage, distinguished only by setup), idempotency replay on ship/pick/complete, BR-10 shipment-cost margin-only invariant, BR-11 no-double-deduct at discrete completion, BR-12 output reversal via variance_gain, BR-6 one-lot-per-batch invariant, cost-basis propagation (material weighted-average, product BOM cost-walk, null-cost rejection), expected_qty event-driven deltas across release/complete/cancel, batch-mode invariants and direct-parent rejection, allocation bucket transitions, races (concurrent pick, dual-MO cost basis race, output-allocation race), discrete completion missing-pick guard, and outputDisposition='blocked' downstream wait. Lane distribution: 7 fast, 15 slow. Every scenario cites contract BR IDs, state-model transition IDs, source-file evidence, and an explicit bug class.

evidence.reason: Phase 1 grounded business rules with code citations.

evidence.symbol: transitions T_PICK_TO_FULL_FIFO, T_COMPLETE_DISCRETE, T_BATCH_COMPLETE, T_OUTPUT_REVERSE, T_SHIP_NORMAL, T_COST_EDIT, T_MATERIALISE_MO_PROMISE
evidence.reason: Phase 2 transitions and blocked transitions used to anchor scenarios.
Existing slow story used as breadth model for new slow scenarios.
Existing fast spec uses /outputs and /outputs reversal; canonical fast write-path style.
Existing invariant style — diffProjections, COUNT(lots) per batch, allocation status counts.

inferences: Wait-for-MO returns the same SalesError 409 negativeStock payload as plain shortage (state-model T_SHIP_NORMAL failure_modes plus revised note). Tests discriminate by setup state, not by response body.
BR-10 must be asserted with explicit counts: COUNT(inventory_events) and COUNT(stock_allocations) snapshots before and after the cost edit must be identical.

BR-11 must assert: COUNT(manufacturing_pick_allocations) for the MO is unchanged across /complete, and the inventory_events at /complete are only manufacturing_output (no manufacturing_pick or sales_consumption).

BR-12 (output reversal) is observed via three independent invariants: (a) produced lot row quantity decremented, (b) ingredient lot quantities restocked equal to the reversal proportion, (c) inventory_events with subtype 'manufacturing_variance_gain' written for the restocked lots.

Idempotency replay must compare the response body and the COUNT of relevant ledger rows (inventory_events, manufacturing_pick_allocations, inventory_lot_balances mutations) between first and second call.
Concurrency scenarios MUST live in slow specs and fire two requests via Promise.allSettled, then assert exactly one 2xx and the appropriate child-row counts.
unknowns: Exact UI selectors for the /execute page Mark done / Complete order / Complete batch buttons. Slow scenarios will need to look these up during test authoring (Phase 4).

Whether reverseManufacturingOutputInTx errors with a clean 400 when the produced lot is already partly consumed by a downstream ship. Scenario S07 includes a precondition that the produced lot is NOT yet consumed, so the canonical reversal path is exercised first.
The exact body shape for batch-mode /outputs route (T_OUTPUT_RECORD_BATCH). The contract notes this is rarely exercised; the scenarios stick to T_BATCH_COMPLETE for batch lot creation.

scenario_groups.why_this_category_matters: End-to-end MO -> SO ship flows are how the feature actually creates value. Each transition is correct individually but the chain must preserve cost basis, expected_qty deltas, allocation bucket movement, and SO/MO state transitions. Bugs here cause silent inventory drift across modules.

scenarios.title: Discrete MO happy path: release -> pick -> complete -> downstream SO ship
scenarios.narrative: A confirmed SO is linked to a discrete MO. After release, the MO picks all ingredients, completes (producing one lot), and the SO's planned shipment ships and consumes from the produced lot. Asserts the full chain: ingredient demand allocations close, expected_qty for the product rises after release and zeros at complete, the produced lot has non-null unitCost, the MO-source allocation materialises onto the produced lot via T_MATERIALISE_MO_PROMISE, and ship consumes the lot hold first (not FIFO). This is the core regression path that every other scenario builds on.
setup: Confirmed SO with one product line linked to a discrete MO
MO already released so ingredient demand allocations are active and expected_qty contribution exists for the product
Sufficient ingredient stock to fully pick without negative-stock or requirement overrides
trigger_sequence: POST /pick on every ingredient with Idempotency-Key
POST /complete with actualQuantity = plannedQuantity and outputDisposition='available'
POST /shipments to plan a shipment for the SO line
expected_user_outcomes: All pick responses 200 and ingredient pickStatus='picked'
Complete response 200; MO row status='done', completedAt set, actualCostPerUnit non-null
Ship response 200; shipment.status='shipped', shippedAt non-null; parent SO status='done'
expected_side_effects: Exactly one new lots row for the produced product with unitCost > 0
manufacturing_pick_allocations rows for every ingredient summing to plannedQuantity each
stock_allocations(demandType='manufacturing_order_ingredient') for this MO have status='consumed'

stock_allocations(demandType='sales_shipment_line', sourceType='inventory_lot') exists pointing to the produced lot AFTER /complete materialises the MO promise; that row's status flips to 'consumed' after ship
inventory_expected_summary contribution for this MO is zero after /complete
inventory_events ledger contains subtypes manufacturing_pick (one per ingredient), manufacturing_complete (one for the produced lot), sales_ship/shipped (one for the shipment line)

evidence.reason: Lines 607-747 — produces lot, releases expected supply, materialises MO source allocations.
Lines 540-823 — held holds first then FIFO.

scenarios.why_prioritized: Regression-class smoke for the entire feature. If this fails the feature is broken end-to-end.

scenarios.title: Batch-mode MO: per-batch start -> pick -> complete -> parent flips only on final batch
scenarios.narrative: A batch-mode MO with 2 batches is released. Each batch is started, picked, and completed independently. Asserts BR-6 (exactly one lot per batch) and that the parent MO status remains 'open' until the final T_BATCH_COMPLETE flips it via T_PARENT_DONE. Asserts every manufacturing_order_batches row gets a distinct lotId and that no batch directly fires a /complete on the parent.
setup: Released batch-mode MO with manufacturingMode='batch' and exactly 2 batches in BATCH_PENDING
Sufficient ingredient stock for both batches
expected_user_outcomes: After batch1 complete: batch1.status='completed', batch1.lotId set, parent MO.status='open'
After batch2 complete: batch2.status='completed', batch2.lotId set (distinct from batch1), parent MO.status='done'
expected_side_effects: Exactly 2 distinct lot rows referenced by the two batches (one per batch — BR-6)
manufacturing_order_outputs has 2 rows, each linked to a different batch and a different lotId
parent MO.completedAt set ONLY after batch2 complete
inventory_expected_summary contribution for the MO is zero after final batch complete (BR-5)

evidence.reason: Lines 5842-6199 — flips parent only on allCompleted; lines 6095-6108 produce without lotId so each batch creates a new lot.

scenarios.why_prioritized: BR-6 / BR-7 are mutually exclusive at the API surface. Regression risk is high because the two completion paths share kernel helpers.

scenarios.title: Wait-for-MO 409 on ship: same SalesError payload as plain shortage, distinguished by setup
scenarios.narrative: A confirmed SO has a planned shipment whose line is allocated against an active 'manufacturing_order' source promise (the MO has been released but not yet produced). The operator attempts to ship. Asserts BR-14: the ship returns 409 with the SAME SalesError negativeStock payload as a plain stock_shortage, even though the actual reason is the unmaterialised MO promise. After the MO completes (producing the lot and materialising the promise via T_MATERIALISE_MO_PROMISE), the same ship request succeeds. This is the production hot spot that confuses ops because the response shape is identical to plain shortage.
setup: Confirmed SO line allocated to an unproduced released MO (stock_allocations sourceType='manufacturing_order', status='active' on the shipment line)
No other free stock available for the product so plain FIFO would also fail
Planned shipment exists covering the SO line
trigger_sequence: POST /shipments/[id]/ship with confirmNegativeStock=true — STILL expect 409 (wait-for-MO guard is BEFORE the negative-stock branch per state-model blocked_transition)
Complete the MO (pick + complete) to materialise the promise onto the produced lot
expected_user_outcomes: First ship attempt: 409 with negativeStock payload {itemId, itemName, available, requested, shortage}
Second ship attempt with override: STILL 409 (override does not bypass wait-for-MO guard)
Third ship attempt after MO complete: 200 success
expected_side_effects: First two attempts: no inventory_events written, no allocation rows mutated, shipment still SHIPMENT_PLANNED
After MO complete: stock_allocations row for the shipment line flips from sourceType='manufacturing_order' to sourceType='inventory_lot' against the produced lot
Third attempt: shipment.status='shipped', allocation row status='consumed'

evidence.reason: Lines 756-768 — InsufficientStockError raised BEFORE FIFO fall-through when a shipment line has an open 'manufacturing_order' source allocation.
Same response shape as plain shortage.

scenarios.why_prioritized: Distinct 409 surface that shares the response shape with plain shortage. The 'same payload, different cause' bug class has caused production support escalations.

scenarios.title: outputDisposition='blocked' bypasses materialisation; downstream ship 409s until released
scenarios.narrative: A discrete MO produces output with outputDisposition='blocked'. The downstream shipment line has an active MO-source allocation. Asserts BR-13: produceManufacturedStockInTx skips materializeManufacturingOrderSourceAllocationsForLotInTx, so the MO-source allocation stays active and the downstream ship still 409s (wait-for-MO) even though a lot for this MO now exists.
setup: Confirmed SO line allocated to released MO (sourceType='manufacturing_order' active)
Planned shipment for the SO line
expected_user_outcomes: Output record + complete both succeed; produced lot exists
Ship returns 409 SalesError negativeStock (wait-for-MO)
expected_side_effects: Produced lot row exists with disposition='blocked' on its inventory_lot_balances row
stock_allocations(demandType='sales_shipment_line', sourceType='manufacturing_order') for this shipment remain status='active' (NOT materialised)
No stock_allocations row of sourceType='inventory_lot' against the produced lot for this shipment line
scenarios.why_prioritized: BR-13 is a subtle invariant; a regression would silently let blocked output feed downstream demand.

scenario_groups.why_this_category_matters: Pick and ship each raise distinct 409 surfaces that share a response shape with similar 409s. Tests must dispatch on the discriminator (warningType for pick; setup state for ship's wait-for-MO vs plain shortage), retry with the correct flag, and never confuse the override paths. These flows have caused production bugs.

Asserts BR-3b: POST /pick returns 409 ManufacturingError with shortage.warningType='requirement_violation' and a nextEligibleDate. Retrying with confirmRequirementOverride=true succeeds; the manufacturing_pick_allocations row carries requirementOverrideConfirmed metadata.

Second attempt: 200 with ingredient pickStatus='picked'

Second attempt: 200; shipment.status='shipped'
expected_side_effects: First attempt: no inventory_events written for the shipment, shipment still SHIPMENT_PLANNED
Second attempt: a NEG-* synthetic lot exists for the product with unitCost > 0
Inventory event of subtype 'sales_ship'/'shipped' written

scenarios.title: Discrete /complete with unpicked ingredients returns 400 listing missing items
scenarios.narrative: Operator hits /complete on a discrete MO before all ingredients are picked. Asserts the missing-pick guard: 400 with error message listing the unpicked ingredient name(s); MO status remains 'open'; no inventory_events written.

scenario_groups.why_this_category_matters: Cost basis (material currentStockUnitCost, product BOM cost-walk, weighted-average on produced lots) and expected_qty deltas drive customer-visible cost figures and supply planning. Drift is silent and accumulates.

items.currentStockUnitCost=10.000000

Inventory event written for the positive flow
scenarios.why_prioritized: Material cost basis underpins every produced lot cost; drift here propagates to every MO.

scenarios.title: Product BOM cost-walk produces non-null unitCost on MO output lot
scenarios.narrative: A discrete MO produces a product whose BOM ingredients each have a known currentStockUnitCost. Asserts BR-4b: the produced lot's unitCost = (sum of ingredient costs consumed + overheadCostTotal) / outputQuantity at scale 6, and matches manufacturing_orders.actualCostPerUnit.

Inventory event of subtype 'manufacturing_complete' carries the same unitCost
scenarios.why_prioritized: Customer-visible cost figure; underpins margin reporting.

scenarios.narrative: A product has no active BOM (or BOM has missing material cost basis). The operator attempts to ship into negative stock with confirmNegativeStock=true. (If/when the route catches MissingCostBasisError, this scenario should be revised to expect a 400/409 with reason='product_bom_cost'.)
setup: Product with NO active BOM ingredients (or with a cyclic BOM)
Confirmed SO for that product with quantity exceeding available stock
Planned shipment for the SO

expected_side_effects: No NEG-* lot created
No inventory_events written for the shipment
shipment.status remains 'planned'
scenarios.why_prioritized: Edge case but a known gap in the response surface; tracks the 500 leak.

scenarios.title: Expected supply deltas across release / output / complete / cancel
scenarios.narrative: Walks one product item through the full event-driven expected_qty lifecycle. Asserts BR-5: release writes 'manufacturing_release' increase; recording output writes 'manufacturing_complete' release of min(currentOpenQty, outputQuantity); discrete /complete fires releaseRemainingExpectedOutputInTx to zero the residual; cancel of a released-only MO reverses the increase.
setup: Product item with zero current expected_qty
Two discrete MOs ready for release (MO-A and MO-B)
trigger_sequence: Pick MO-A ingredients then record output for partial quantity; record expectedQty drop
expected_user_outcomes: After release of MO-A: items.expectedQty == plannedA
After release of MO-B: items.expectedQty == plannedA + plannedB
After partial output on MO-A (qty=outA): items.expectedQty == (plannedA - outA) + plannedB
After /complete on MO-A: items.expectedQty == plannedB (residual MO-A expected fully released)
After /delete on MO-B: items.expectedQty == 0
expected_side_effects: inventory_events ledger contains subtypes manufacturing_release (twice), manufacturing_complete (twice — output + completion), and manufacturing_cancel/release for the deleted MO
No drift between items.expectedQty and the sum of active expected_increase/release events for this item
scenarios.why_prioritized: Inventory planning depends on items.expectedQty being a faithful function of MO state. Drift here breaks MRP-lite.

scenario_groups.why_this_category_matters: MO and shipment state machines must reject invalid transitions at the API surface and produce exactly-once side effects on valid ones. Mis-routed transitions silently corrupt the ledger.

scenarios.title: Output reversal: negative /outputs decrements produced lot and restocks ingredient lots via manufacturing_variance_gain
scenarios.narrative: After recording a positive output and BEFORE downstream consumption, the operator submits POST /outputs with negative quantity. Asserts BR-12: reverseManufacturingOutputInTx (a) decrements the produced lot quantity, (b) restocks the originally-consumed ingredient lots by the reversal proportion, and (c) writes inventory_events with eventType/subtype 'manufacturing_variance_gain' for each ingredient restock. manufacturing_orders.actualQuantity/actualMaterialCost/actualCostPerUnit are recomputed from surviving outputs.

expected_side_effects: Produced lot row quantity decremented by 3 (from 10 to 7)
Each originally-consumed ingredient lot row has its quantity restored by 30% of the originally-consumed amount (proportional reversal)
inventory_events with eventType='manufacturing_variance_gain' written for each restocked ingredient lot
manufacturing_orders.actualMaterialCost and actualCostPerUnit recomputed from surviving output rows
manufacturing_order_outputs has 2 rows now: the original +10 and the new -3 (or whichever shape the kernel uses)
scenarios.why_prioritized: BR-12 is high-confidence in the contract but the test must assert the THREE independent invariants (lot decrement, ingredient restock, variance_gain events). Often missed in coverage.

expected_user_outcomes: Response 200; MO status='done'
expected_side_effects: COUNT(manufacturing_pick_allocations) for this MO is identical to the pre-complete snapshot

scenario_groups.why_this_category_matters: BR-10 (shipment cost margin-only) is silently load-bearing: a regression that lets cost edits touch inventory or AP would corrupt Xero invoices. This must be asserted as the ABSENCE of side effects.

scenario_groups.why_this_category_matters: The production hot spots are ship/pick/complete replays and concurrent MOs/picks. Mis-handled idempotency double-effects the ledger; mis-locked rows let two transactions both succeed and corrupt cost basis. All three replay paths must be tested.

R2 = 200 with R2.body === R1.body (cached envelope)
R3 = 409 IdempotencyConflictError

COUNT(inventory_lot_balances mutations) identical
shipment.shippedAt identical between after-R1 and after-R2

scenarios.why_prioritized: Production hot spot. UI ship retries are common; double-effect would silently double-decrement stock.

scenarios.title: Idempotent pick + complete replay: same key returns cached body; no double-deduct
scenarios.narrative: Replay test for pick and complete. (a) POST /pick K1 then POST /pick K1 — second returns cached 200; pick allocations unchanged. (b) POST /complete K2 then POST /complete K2 — second returns cached 200; status='done' unchanged; no second produced lot; actualQuantity unchanged.
setup: Released discrete MO ready for pick
trigger_sequence: POST /pick with key K1 on ingredient I
POST /pick with key K1 on ingredient I again
expected_user_outcomes: Both /pick K1 calls return 200 with identical bodies
Both /complete K2 calls return 200 with identical bodies
expected_side_effects: COUNT(manufacturing_pick_allocations) for ingredient I after second K1 == after first K1
COUNT(manufacturing_order_outputs) for the MO after second K2 == after first K2
Exactly one produced lot row for the MO
manufacturing_orders.actualQuantity stable across the replay
scenarios.why_prioritized: Idempotency replay is the universal safety net; if it fails, every other operation could double-effect on retry.

scenarios.title: Concurrent pick on same ingredient: row lock serialises; exactly one succeeds
scenarios.narrative: Two simultaneous POST /pick requests on the same ingredient (different Idempotency-Keys). The DAL locks the ingredient row FOR UPDATE. Asserts: exactly ONE response is 200; the OTHER is 400 'is already picked'; COUNT(manufacturing_pick_allocations) for the ingredient equals the picks the winning call wrote (not double); ingredient pickStatus='picked' once.
setup: Released discrete MO with one ingredient unpicked
Sufficient stock for one full pick (so both could theoretically succeed if not serialised)
trigger_sequence: Fire two POST /pick requests in parallel via Promise.allSettled with different Idempotency-Keys
expected_user_outcomes: Exactly one response has status 200
The other has status 400 with message containing 'is already picked'
expected_side_effects: COUNT(manufacturing_pick_allocations) for the ingredient equals the FIRST winner's allocation count (not double)
Ingredient row pickStatus='picked' (exactly once)
No partial pick state visible
scenarios.why_prioritized: Concurrency invariants must be tested in real Postgres; mocks would not surface lock-ordering bugs.

scenarios.title: Concurrent /complete on two MOs producing into the same product: cost basis weighted-average reconciles regardless of completion order
scenarios.narrative: MO-A and MO-B both complete and produce into the same product (separate lots in this case because batch-mode creates distinct lots per batch, but the items.currentStockUnitCost weighted-average covers both lots). Lock ordering on items.id via lockItemsInTx serialises the two transactions. Asserts: after both complete, items.currentStockUnitCost equals the cumulative weighted average across both produced lot quantities and costs, regardless of which MO commits first. COUNT(lots) added equals 2 (one per MO). No deadlock observed.
setup: Two released discrete MOs (MO-A, MO-B) producing into the same product item
Both MOs fully picked with non-zero ingredient costs
Snapshot of items.currentStockUnitCost before both completes
trigger_sequence: Fire POST /complete on MO-A and POST /complete on MO-B in parallel via Promise.allSettled
expected_user_outcomes: Both responses are 200
expected_side_effects: Exactly two new lot rows for the product (one per MO)
items.currentStockUnitCost equals the cumulative weighted average: (qtyA*costA + qtyB*costB) / (qtyA + qtyB) at scale 6
Both inventory_events of subtype 'manufacturing_complete' exist with idempotency_key non-null
No transaction failed due to deadlock
scenarios.why_prioritized: Cost basis race is the kind of bug that only manifests under concurrency in production; deterministic tests guard the lock ordering.

review_focus: Are the three 409 surfaces (S05 stock_shortage, S06 requirement_violation, S07 negativeStock) each clearly distinguished by the discriminator the scenario asserts (warningType for pick, negativeStock payload presence for ship), and does S03 explicitly note that wait-for-MO uses the SAME response shape as plain shortage so the test must discriminate by setup?

Is BR-11 (no double deduct at /complete) asserted with the three independent invariants — COUNT(pick_allocations) unchanged, ingredient lot quantities unchanged, no 'manufacturing_pick' events post-complete — rather than a single weak assertion?

Is BR-12 (output reversal) asserted with the three independent invariants — produced lot quantity decremented, ingredient lots restocked, variance_gain events written — and does the scenario explicitly require the lot to NOT yet be consumed downstream?

Is BR-10 (cost margin-only) asserted as the ABSENCE of side effects (COUNT(inventory_events) unchanged, COUNT(stock_allocations) unchanged, no Xero audit row) and not as the presence of the cost rows alone?
Are idempotency replays asserted on response BODY equality AND on ledger COUNT stability, and does the mismatched-key replay (S19) explicitly expect IdempotencyConflictError?
Are concurrency scenarios (S21, S22) using Promise.allSettled with at-most-one-2xx assertions, and asserting child-row counts rather than relying on timing?
